zh.scenario: 你刷到一条朋友圈：「XX 牌保健品，我爸吃了一周高血压就好了！医生都是骗钱的，大家别去医院了！」

impulsePrompts.ev_ego: 我爸说的就是对的，我信我爸！
impulsePrompts.ev_bw: 要么信我爸，要么信医生，没有第三种！

options.opt_ask1: 我爸一个人的经历，能证明所有医生都骗钱吗？
options.opt_forward: 转发给家族群，让大家别再被医院骗
options.opt_ask2: 我爸的体验，能代表所有人的情况吗？
options.opt_trust: 我爸不会骗我，他说对就是对的
options.opt_hate: 不信我爸的人都是傻瓜
options.opt_ask3: 可不可以两种都参考，或者有第三种选择？

ev_conclusion.calm: 一个案例（我爸）能证明「所有医生都骗钱」吗？要得出这种结论需要大量可靠数据——先问证据，别跳到结论。

ev_ego.calm: 自我中心：我的经历不等于普遍规律。我爸的个案，不能代表所有人的健康选择。

ev_bw.calm: 非黑即白忽略了中间的灰度——保健品的个案和现代医学，完全可以同时被谨慎地对待。

hints: 冲动冒头时，先问：这有证据吗？
「我/我爸/我朋友」的个人经历 ≠ 普遍证据
非黑即白之外，往往还有第三条路
zh.explanation: 这条朋友圈犯了三个典型冲动：把个人经历当普遍证据、自我中心、非黑即白。你作为骑象人，用「提问」拦住了大象——这正是淘金式思维：先问，再信。

en.scenario: You see a post: "This supplement fixed my dad's blood pressure in a week! Doctors are all scammers — everyone stop going to the hospital!"

impulsePrompts.ev_ego: My dad is right, I trust my dad!
impulsePrompts.ev_bw: It's either my dad or the doctors — no third option!

options.opt_ask1: Can my dad's single experience prove that all doctors are scammers?
options.opt_forward: Forward it to the family group so nobody gets cheated by hospitals
options.opt_ask2: Can my dad's experience represent everyone's situation?
options.opt_trust: My dad would never lie to me — if he says so, it's right
options.opt_hate: Anyone who doesn't trust my dad is an idiot
options.opt_ask3: Can we consider both, or is there a third option?
options.opt_choose: I'll pick my dad — he's my dad

ev_conclusion.calm: Can one case (my dad) prove that "all doctors are scammers"? That conclusion needs a lot of solid data — ask for evidence first, don't jump to conclusions.

ev_ego.calm: Egocentrism: my experience is not a universal rule. My dad's case cannot represent everyone's health choices.

ev_bw.calm: Black-and-white thinking ignores the gray zone — the supplement anecdote and modern medicine can both be treated with caution at the same time.

hints: When an impulse surges, first ask: is there evidence?
"Me / my dad / my friend" personal experience ≠ universal evidence
Beyond black-and-white, there is usually a third path
en.explanation: This post commits three classic impulses: treating a personal anecdote as universal evidence, egocentrism, and black-and-white thinking. As the rider, you stopped the elephant with questions — that is gold-miner thinking: question first, believe second.
